clue.text: Before you start, this grid is dumb

definitions.text: Before you start, this grid is
definitions.meaning: an empty crossword grid, before any answers are filled in, holds no text at all
dumb in the sense of silent, unable to speak

explanation.surface: A setter teasing the solver: the blank puzzle in front of you has nothing to say yet.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition describes the very grid being solved: before you write anything in, it holds no entries.
explanation.definitionFit: Being speechless or silent is the core sense of the adjective, a straight synonym of mute.

clue.text: Writer brought down by marquess's trick involving duke

indicators.note: involving says the trick's letters take in the duke's

parts.note: a wile is a cunning trick

explanation.surface: A writer ruined by a nobleman's ploy that drew in a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marquess of Queensberry's accusation led to Oscar Wilde's trial and imprisonment in 1895.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde, the Irish playwright, was ruined after suing the Marquess of Queensberry for libel.

clue.text: Easing of hostility briefly limits border damage

indicators.note: limits says the shortened word encloses the border word
briefly says the last letter is cut

parts.note: detente is a relaxing of tension between nations
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A thaw between rivals keeps a lid on harm along the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the final E, leaving DETENT, and 'limits' wraps that round the edge word.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm or injury is the noun's meaning, as in to the detriment of someone.

clue.text: 'Frightful' word that is on line including last letter in book

indicators.note: including says the cry holds that letter

parts.note: eek is a cry of fright
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
IE abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A scary word added to a line that includes the final letter of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last letter' looks like the book's end but means Z, the alphabet's last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament has a prophetic text bearing this prophet's name.

clue.text: Ill-disposed view of din (e.g. cell's noise)?

definitions.text: Ill-disposed view of din (e.g. cell's noise)?

indicators.note: ill-disposed says the letters are badly arranged and must be put in new order

explanation.surface: A grumpy opinion on racket, such as the noise in a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the maxim is an unfriendly view of noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb praises quiet as precious, an attitude hostile to noise.

clue.text: Anti-fur campaigners elected French leader during hostilities

parts.note: PETA, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals, campaigns against fur
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: Animal-rights activists voted in as France's head while the war raged.
explanation.walkthrough: Philippe Pétain headed the Vichy French state during the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshal Pétain led Vichy France during the Second World War, so he is a wartime French head of state.

clue.text: In the end, this grid is something painful to beat

definitions.text: In the end, this grid is

parts.note: a pang is a sharp pain
to ram is to strike or batter

explanation.surface: A setter admitting the finished puzzle hurts to conquer.
explanation.walkthrough: Once completed, this grid uses every letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Text using all twenty-six letters of the alphabet; the finished grid does exactly that.

clue.text: Embittered Bill Bailey's opening in Morecambe, say

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

indicators.note: in says the letter goes within the first name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a British comedian, so Eric is an example of a Morecambe

indicators.note: opening says take the first letter of Bailey

explanation.surface: Comedian Bill Bailey's opening night at the seaside town of Morecambe left him sour.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Bailey is a British comic and Morecambe a Lancashire resort; here Morecambe is Eric Morecambe, the comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp and sour in tone or temper; bitter is the core sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Bad reputation of Rio, not yet prepared

indicators.note: prepared says the letters are reworked, as food is prepared

explanation.surface: The city of Rio gets bad press for being unready, say for the Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well known for something bad, infamy, is the standard sense of the noun.

clue.text: Recoil from circular piece in rotary tool

indicators.note: in says the round letter sits within the tool's name

parts.note: a lathe spins the workpiece to shape it
the letter O is round

explanation.surface: Flinching away from a disc spinning inside a power tool in the workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink back from something in disgust is to detest it, a synonym phrase for strong dislike.

clue.text: Small retreats in lead-up to Easter, which 11 may use to relax 13

indicators.note: in says the backward word sits inside the season's name

parts.note: Lent is the forty days before Easter

indicators.note: retreats says the word for small goes backwards

parts.note: mini means small

explanation.surface: Little spiritual retreats held during Lent, which a masseur might use to loosen a body.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 and 13 are cross-references: 11 is RUBBER (a masseur) and 13 is MUSCLE; 'retreats' turns MINI into INIM.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrocation rubbed into the body by a masseur eases stiffness, so a rubber uses it on tight muscle.

clue.text: Picture report gets backing with Number 6 as prisoner

indicators.note: as prisoner says these letters are held inside the reversed word
gets backing says the word for report is read in reverse

parts.note: a report is a loud noise, like a gunshot
VI is 6 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A TV report revisits The Prisoner, the cult series whose hero is Number 6.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets backing' gives ESION; the Prisoner in the TV series was Number 6, a hint that 'as prisoner' signals holding letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to imagine or visualise it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: What's useful if amending drawings for some bridge?

definitions.meaning: an eraser, used to correct pencil sketches
in the card game bridge, a series of games, best of three

explanation.surface: Asking what helps an architect who keeps redrawing plans for a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' looks like a structure to be drawn, but it is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: British English calls an eraser this; in bridge the word names a best-of-three set of games.

clue.text: A wake-up call brought round someone of faith wanting lead and accepting Lord's

indicators.note: accepting says the reversed word takes in another letter
brought round says the shortened word is turned backwards
wanting lead says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a believer is a person with religious faith
L is an abbreviation for Lord

explanation.surface: A devotee, roused by a morning call, comes round to the Lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting lead' leaves ELIEVER, 'brought round' turns it to REVEILE, and 'accepting' takes in the L.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call that rouses soldiers in the morning is the classic military wake-up signal.

clue.text: Cayenne's what since stopping putrefaction makes a strong dairy product

indicators.note: stopping says those letters plug the middle of the decay word

parts.note: rot is decay
que is French for what, spoken in Cayenne, capital of French Guiana
for can mean since or because

explanation.surface: A chef asks what cayenne pepper can do to halt decay in a powerful cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Cayenne looks like the pepper but is the French Guianese city, so its language is French.
explanation.definitionFit: This pungent blue French ewe's milk cheese is a strong-tasting dairy product.

clue.text: Clout helping to make ignoramus clever

indicators.note: helping to make says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Power and influence can turn even a dunce into someone smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout as power or influence matches the figurative sense of strength or force to get one's way.

clue.text: Low character in screenplay for Das Boot?

indicators.note: for says the screenplay is written for the vessel, which comes first

parts.note: Das Boot is a German film about a U-boat crew, so the boat is a sub
a script is the text of a film

explanation.surface: A villainous role in the script of the U-boat film Das Boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low character' suggests a villain but means a small character printed below the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A character set below the line of text, as in chemical formulae, is literally low.

clue.text: 'Tender parts' or what you see cradling them?

definitions.meaning: price estimates, the key parts of a tender for a contract
the inverted commas around the words Tender parts in the clue

explanation.surface: Sore body parts, and a question about what is holding them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' suggests soreness, but it is a bid for a contract; the second definition points at the punctuation printed round those words.
explanation.definitionFit: Price estimates make up a contract bid, and the punctuation marks enclosing printed words share the same name.

clue.text: Demand too much of green area to feed farm animal

indicators.note: to feed says those letters go into the animal's mouth, inside its name

parts.note: an ox is a farm beast
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: Asking a lot of a patch of grassland to sustain livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain beyond capacity or exhaust by excessive requirements is the verb's meaning.

clue.text: State of bluegrass filling grassy area up

indicators.note: filling says the state's letters sit inside the turf word

parts.note: a sward is a stretch of turf
Kentucky, the Bluegrass State, abbreviated KY

explanation.surface: Kentucky's bluegrass filling a meadow that is sprouting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading towards the heavens, upwards, is the direction this adverb names.

clue.text: Learner's inside changing his baby in worn-out mode

indicators.note: inside says the learner's letter is placed within the rest
changing says the letters of his baby are rearranged

parts.note: L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A trainee parent is changing his baby's nappy, looking rather worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' looks like nappy-changing but rearranges HIS BABY to SHABBIY, and the L goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a threadbare, worn manner is the adverb's meaning, describing shabby condition.

clue.text: Messed around, keeping Juliet put off

indicators.note: keeping says the jumble holds that letter
messed says the letters of around are jumbled

parts.note: J is Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo fooled about while keeping Juliet waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messed around' reads as a single phrase, but 'Messed' shuffles AROUND into ADOURN, which then holds J.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone a meeting until later, to defer, is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Special Constable taken off landscape to protect good life

indicators.note: to protect says what is left wraps round another letter
taken off says those two letters are removed

parts.note: landscape means scenery
SC is the abbreviation for a Special Constable, a British volunteer police officer

explanation.surface: A volunteer police officer is removed from the countryside to safeguard a decent existence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken off' leaves ENERY; 'to protect' wraps that round G. 'life' means vigour, not existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Life in the sense of vigour or liveliness, as in full of life, is vitality and drive.

clue.text: Dissident died in Montmartre, first person caught on hill

parts.note: OB, short for Latin obiit, means died
je is French for I, the first person, as spoken in Paris's Montmartre
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A rebel dies in Paris, the first to be arrested on the hill of Montmartre.
explanation.walkthrough: Montmartre is a hill district of Paris, so 'in Montmartre' signals French.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter is one who protests or refuses to conform, a synonym for someone raising objections.

clue.text: Perhaps Emerson, Lake & Palmer initially welcomed by a cheer

indicators.note: welcomed by says the letters go inside the cheer

parts.note: rah is a cheer, as in hurrah

indicators.note: initially says take the first letters of Lake and Palmer

explanation.surface: The prog-rock trio Emerson, Lake & Palmer greeted with applause.
explanation.walkthrough: Emerson looks like the keyboardist Keith but is Ralph Waldo Emerson, the American essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American essayist, so his first name is an example of this given name.

clue.text: Old tub moved by means of propulsion attached at the back?

definitions.text: Old tub moved by means of propulsion attached at the back?

indicators.note: moved says the three letters of tub are shuffled

parts.note: an oar propels a rowing boat

indicators.note: at the back picks the final letter of attached

explanation.surface: An old boat driven by a motor clamped to its stern.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'moved' turns TUB into UTB, and 'at the back' takes the D of 'attached'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat powered by a detachable motor clamped to the stern is called by this word.

clue.text: Place of relief, having home swamped by Russian river

indicators.note: swamped by says the home word is engulfed by the river's name

parts.note: the Ural is a river in Russia
at home means in

explanation.surface: Finding refuge after a house is flooded by a river in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A gents' toilet fixture is where one relieves oneself, so relief here is bodily.

clue.text: Time ran out, leaving one written to tersely

indicators.note: leaving says that letter departs from the word

parts.note: exited means went out
I is one as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: The clock ran down, so someone got only a curt note.
explanation.walkthrough: EXITED loses I to give EXTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent a short phone message, the clipped style of mobile messaging being terse.

clue.text: Small-scale work revised the canon

indicators.note: revised says the letters of the phrase are reworked into new order

explanation.surface: A minor piece of scholarship reworks the accepted body of texts.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineering at the scale of molecules and atoms is the tiniest technology there is.
